messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: ggplot2 development dependencies
parts:
Hi all,

As fixes to ggplot2 bug sometimes require changes in dependent
packages, I've been thinking about how best to capture these
dependencies. Currently I only assign new version numbers just before
a package is released - this is mainly due to my informal release
process, where I don't in advance whether a version will be a major or
minor increment. This means that (e.g.) the scales package does not
change version numbers until it is released to cran, and there's
currently no way to state that ggplot2 needs a development version of
scales.

What I'm proposing is that whenever I make a change in the scales
package because of ggplot2, I'll increment the version number in
scales, and then in ggplot2's description file. This may mean that
version numbers on cran are non-contiguous, but it will ensure that
people using the dev version are always alerted to updates to
dependencies.

What do you think?

Hadley

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 development dependencies
parts:
I think that makes a lot of sense, and is exactly what minor
increments are for. Something like 0.2.01, 0.2.02, etc. it provides a
nice way to make the changes you need and allow dependencies.

Josh
